correctness.rationale: For positive edge resistances, each diagonal of the inverse grounded Laplacian is an effective resistance to the two pinned vertices. Tree series-parallel reduction gives \(h+z(\ell-z)/\ell\), with h the off-path resistance and z the coordinate on the leader path of length ell. All unordered leader pairs reduce to eight orbits; the table in RESULT.md is obtained by explicit sum. Same-side leaf pairs and opposite-side leaf pairs strictly exceed the both-hub cost for \(p,q\ge2,\ t>0\). A same-side hub-leaf pair is strictly worse than the corresponding cross-hub-leaf pair by \(t[1+(q+1)t]/(t+1)\) or \(t[1+(p+1)t]/(t+1)\). The remaining lower envelope is \(N+\min\{0,[t(\min\{p,q\}-1)-1]/(t+1)\}\), yielding every equality case at the exact boundary. The embedded exact-rational verifier independently evaluates 4700 actual grounded inverses and 15 transition checks; these computations supplement but do not replace the analytic proof.

value.rationale: A pair of branching hubs joined by a tunable communication link is a minimal heterogeneous network where the best sensor/leader locations need not coincide with the two high-degree hubs. The theorem provides a complete natural two-parameter family classification over integer leaf multiplicities and positive bridge resistance, a sharp transition at the reciprocal minority leaf count, and all optimizer ties. It explains the counterintuitive regime in which pinning a peripheral leaf is preferable to pinning the second hub, with relevance to placement under changing intercluster connectivity. Its value is the structural threshold and complete classification, not merely correctness of finite matrix inversions.
